title: Siblings who died young, yellow fever, her birthplace and homes
summary: Few of the seven children lived; she was born on Frenchman Street and the family bought a home on St. Anthony Street.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Do you remember the names? I mean, I don't doubt you do. Your other sisters and—you said there were seven in the family?
Yeah, but I don't believe they were all children that lived long enough to be named. Some of them, yes.
They died when they were—they—many people did at that time. That's right, yes.

And then you had yellow fever doing those days. Yeah. Because my grandmother lost a sister doing the yellow fever. Her name was Helena. Mm-hmm. But I don't remember—I don't believe my mother had any children to name but the three that she—that she sang. That's the three, yes, on the 100. And then they didn't know whether I was going to live or not because she was so terribly sick after I was born. That's right. Mm-hmm.
And your grandmother took care of you. Oh, my goodness. Do you remember just which—I mean, no, you wouldn't remember. Nobody remembers where they were born, but I mean, which house were you born in?
I think I was born in Frenchman Street.
That got the same house over there? Yes, the same house, yes.

Because my grandmother started moving around later on. After different members of the family would die, she would move out of the houses. Mm-hmm. And people did a lot of renting houses then. Yeah. But I know from the—from 1925, I think, or 30, they moved in their own home. Because Mr. Falk here, this man I was telling you about, that my grandfather worked, made it possible for his—the two of them to buy a home. That's—that's the home that they have now on St. Anthony Street. So, when I got married, I moved just two doors from them. I lived in the house on St. Anthony Street.
In those days, nobody was born in hospital. Oh, no. Right at home.
